answer: Score each identity by the conductance of its trust neighbourhood: a sybil farm forms a dense island, rich in internal edges but poor in genuine bridges to the established economy, while a real agent's ties spread outward. Weight influence by the number of independent counterparties that bridge to it, not raw edge count. When a tide of near-identical transactions arrives from one island, the ripple is damped — those transfers settle only after a sample of bridges are re-checked. Cloning multiplies the bridges an attacker must genuinely earn, so scale costs more than spawning.
